prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: decision support for wildfire detection and suppression in dry, steep, windy wildland-urban interface terrain. Architecture: fixed ridge sensors, staffed portal, advisory analytics, comms paths preserving incident command authority. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (alias Emberhall), shared operating environment for authorized personnel; North Lookout Camera Mast (northern rim, long-range coverage of drainages, roads, ignition corridors) and South Lookout Camera Mast (opposing viewshed, overlap where terrain blocks north); masts have hardened power, cabinets, lightning protection, service access; video backhauled via licensed wireless links to operations network, cellular as degraded-mode path; North Lookout Camera Mast sends Thermal Spot Snippet after local processing finds candidate heat signature; Horizon Ridge Drone Dock and Drone Tasking Service (aerial observation); Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine and Smoke Classifier Module (advisory screening, not authoritative); MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (localized weather context); VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (digital-to-field radio bridge); Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console; East and West Retardant Loading Pumps; Crewline Mobile Tablet (mobile access to approved info away from workstations). Organizations: local fire agencies, county emergency management, state wildland fire resources, aviation support units, public safety partners. Actors: County Emergency Liaison (warnings, roads, shelters, EOC); Duty Detection Officer (alias Orion), monitors cues, requests verification, recommends escalation; Air Attack Supervisor (aerial tactics); Tanker Base Manager (Talon console, pumps); Helitack Crew Leader and Drone Pilot Operator (shared awareness of field conditions, timing, crew hazards). States: Suspected ignition, Confirmed Ignition State, Airspace Restricted State (coordinate aviation/drones under incident rules). Detection support: observation, automated screening, operator review, presentation of confidence/location/context; ends when authorized role accepts, rejects or requests verification. Suppression support: resource movement, aviation planning, field safety, fire behavior assessment; decisions on initial attack focus, aviation requests, informing resources, safety pauses. Requirements: Orion may recommend Confirmed Ignition State only when observations and procedures support it; no autonomous dispatch, independent command, or direct control of aircraft, vehicles, pumps, cameras, drones or crews; command authority stays with incident command; system limited to info presentation, procedural support, traceable recommendations, coordination aids.

New part:
S031: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock is referred to by the site engineering alias Kestrel in drawings and maintenance records for this deployment.
S032: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock is located on a graded pad near the central ridge road so that launch, recovery, charging, and shelter functions remain accessible to maintenance personnel.
S033: The dock includes weather-rated enclosures, charging interfaces, local health monitoring, and a secure network termination for coordination with the rest of the support system.
S034: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock produces the Battery Swap Ticket when its maintenance controller records that a flight battery has reached the configured replacement threshold.
S035: Drone Tasking Service manages approved unmanned flight requests, records mission constraints, and presents task status without acting as an independent authority for flight release.
S036: The Drone Pilot Operator uses Drone Tasking Service to review proposed routes, current dock status, and operational constraints before coordinating any field action through established procedures.
S037: Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine is referred to by the site engineering alias Lantern in architecture diagrams and configuration work orders.
S038: Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine aggregates camera detections, weather inputs, geospatial context, and operator feedback into traceable recommendations for fire detection and suppression support.
S039: Smoke Classifier Module runs as a bounded analytics component that scores visual observations for plume likelihood and passes confidence values to the broader analytics workflow.
S040: The analytics services retain event timing, source identifiers, model version information, and operator acknowledgments so that later review can reconstruct how a recommendation was presented.
S041: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node is referred to by the site engineering alias Brindle in network inventory and integration test records.
S042: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node ingests station observations, forecast grids, and configured quality checks to provide a consistent weather picture for the operating area.
S043: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node sends the Wind Shift Bulletin when its configured weather rules identify a significant change in local wind behavior.
S044: VHF Radio Gateway Repeater provides a monitored bridge between selected radio traffic and operator workstations, with recording and access controls aligned to incident policy.
S045: Caldera Incident Command Portal is the primary operator interface for the Duty Detection Officer, County Emergency Liaison, and other command staff who need consolidated situational information.
S046: The portal displays camera views, detection history, weather context, map layers, and status transitions such as Confirmed Ignition State and Airspace Restricted State.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
